critiques.title: Use the same species colors in the ranking and trend views
critiques.issue: Species identity changes visual treatment across the two data charts: the trend chart assigns distinct colors to the three focal birds, but the ranking chart uses one uniform bar color for all birds.
critiques.rationale: When readers compare the most-spotted birds with the long-term trend lines, they must re-learn which species are being emphasized. Carrying the same species colors across both panels would make the cross-panel story easier to follow.

critiques.suggestion: Color the three focal species in the ranking chart with the same hues used in the trend chart and mute the remaining birds in a neutral tone.

critiques.rationale: For an indexed line chart focused on relative change over time, a zero baseline is not required the way it is for bars. Using a domain closer to the observed range makes the divergence between declining and stable species easier to see without changing the underlying values.
